_about: Rules for app/ocr/pipeline.py. Each section says when a step is advised and how strong it is, aimed at what PaddleOCR (through RapidOCR) actually sees. These are starting guesses, not measured values: tune them against real pages and record the evidence beside each value. Grey levels run from 0 (black) to 255 (white).

analysis._what: How the page is measured. Ink is any pixel clearly darker than the paper right around it; the paper is found with a kernel this share of the page's shorter side, which must be wider than the characters. Contrast and ink level come from the darkest stroke_core_share of ink pixels (the core of the strokes). Tilt and the text area are worked out on a copy long_side_px on its longer side.

crop._what: Advised when a large part of the page holds no marks at all AND cropping lets Paddle shrink the page noticeably less (by at least min_scale_gain). Paddle shrinks any image longer than its size limit before reading, so empty margins along the long side make it shrink the text too. Cropping only the short side changes nothing for Paddle: in the 15-page run, such crops moved confidence by noise only (-0.012 to +0.003). The crop keeps every mark plus a margin of a few character heights.

denoise._what: Advised when the plain paper shows grain. Strength = noise x strength_per_sigma, capped at max_strength.

deskew._what: Advised when the text lines are tilted by at least min_tilt_deg and straightening makes them clearly more distinct. Paddle's detector copes with small tilts on its own, so small ones are left alone. A tilt found at the search limit is not trusted.

flatten_light._what: Advised when the paper brightness varies across the text area AND the paper is not already white, which is what a shadow on photographed paper looks like. On white paper, variation comes from dark print or boxes instead: in the 15-page run, flattening those did nothing or harm (Picture2 -0.035), while on grey photographed paper it helped (Capture +0.013, receipt_1 +0.019). The kernel is a few character heights wide so it erases text and keeps the lighting.

stretch_contrast._what: Advised when ink and paper are too close in brightness (faded print). Maps the measured ink and paper levels onto the targets. Set to 0, which switches it off: on every page it fired on, across every run, it lowered Paddle's confidence (Picture4.jpg, -0.014 to -0.055) and never once helped. Raise below_text_contrast above 0 to test it again.

brighten._what: Advised when the paper is dark and neither flatten_light nor stretch_contrast already fixes it. A gamma below 1 lifts the paper towards target_paper_level.

resize._what: Paddle cuts each text line out and resizes it to 48 px tall for reading, after first shrinking any image longer than its size limit (2000 px by default), and its detector already enlarges small images. So enlarging is OFF (below_text_height_px 0): in the 15-page run, enlarging on its own never helped (Picture3 -0.006, Picture5 -0.014, Picture6 -0.004) and took about 1.7x longer. Raise below_text_height_px above 0 to test it again. When on, it is never taken past Paddle's size limit, because Paddle would shrink it straight back. size_basis 'small' sizes for the small characters (10th percentile); 'median' for typical text.

sharpen._what: Advised when the edges around the text are soft. The further below the threshold, the stronger, from min_amount to max_amount. Kept strict because sharpening a JPEG photo also sharpens its artefacts.

adaptive_threshold._what: Black and white by local threshold. Advised only when text contrast is below below_text_contrast. Set to 0, which switches it off: in the earlier runs it lowered Paddle's confidence on both images (0.861 -> 0.797 and 0.909 -> 0.867). Paddle's models were trained on ordinary greyscale and colour images, not black-and-white ones.
